description:
principal.rs:47-59 — utcStart and utcEnd are extracted from the wire and immediately validated via UTCDate::new_validated() with explicit invalidArguments mapping. Client-supplied malformed values do NOT flow into the backend.

This is the right pattern for the wire boundary. Naive code might:
- (a) Accept any string and let the backend deal with it → backend sees malformed input, has to decide how to fail, leaks impl details into the error.
- (b) Use Default UTCDate parsing inside the typed struct → invariant only enforced inside type's own deserialize, not at the handler.

The chosen pattern explicitly validates at the boundary, maps to a spec-defined error code, and threads the validated UTCDate into the backend. The bd:JMAP-sc1b.70 commit (4c8a76a) deliberately introduced this pattern across mail-server and calendars-server.

A future contributor might suggest 'simplify by passing &str to the backend' — that would re-create the old bug. Defend the validated-at-boundary pattern.
title: Principal/getAvailability uses UTCDate::new_validated at the wire boundary
